analysis: The code snippet is inside a `synchronized` block on `videoListeners`. It calls `videoListeners.toArray(new VideoListener[videoListeners.size()])`. The `toArray` javadoc declares two exceptions: `NullPointerException` (if the specified array is null) and `ArrayStoreException` (if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of every element in the list). The array passed is a newly created `VideoListener[]` of size equal to the current list size, so it is never null. Therefore, `NullPointerException` is avoided. `ArrayStoreException` occurs if any element in the list has a runtime type that is not a subtype of `VideoListener`. The code does not perform any check on the actual types of elements in `videoListeners`. Although the list is likely typed as `List<VideoListener>`, type erasure at runtime could allow non-`VideoListener` objects if the list was used with raw types or unchecked casts. Since no validation is present, the condition for `ArrayStoreException` is not fully avoided.
remark: `ArrayStoreException` may be thrown if the `videoListeners` list contains an element whose runtime type is not assignable to `VideoListener` (e.g., due to heap pollution from raw types or unchecked operations). The code does not validate the list contents before calling `toArray`, so this exception is possible.
